title: 19 Things That Make You A Pushover
author: Linsin, Michael
summary: Michael Linsin argues that students make an instant assessment on the first day of school about whether their teacher will hold the line — and that the teacher's own observable behaviors, not student intentions, determine the outcome. He lists 19 specific signals that mark a teacher as a pushover: from failing to teach rules on day one, to ignoring minor misbehavior, to reminding rather than enforcing consequences. The underlying premise is that misbehavior is not students' preference but an almost inevitable response when the classroom lacks firm, clear leadership. Linsin closes with a counterintuitive point — despite initial resistance and testing, students actually want strong direction, high standards, and discipline, because being held accountable is itself evidence that someone cares about them.
points: Students read teacher behavior on day one to determine whether the teacher is a pushover — the assessment is driven by the teacher's observable conduct (vague expectations, ignoring minor misbehavior, reminding instead of enforcing) rather than any prior intention by students to misbehave.

The distinction between reminding and enforcing is central to Linsin's framework: reminding signals that consequences are negotiable and repeated, while enforcing signals that the rules are real and consistent — the two generate completely different classroom cultures over time.

Physical and environmental signals matter as much as verbal ones: a messy desk, unprofessional dress, nervous pacing, and erratic supervision all communicate reduced authority before a word is spoken.

Linsin's most counterintuitive claim is that misbehavior is not students' first choice — it is what fills the vacuum when a teacher fails to provide the structure, inspiration, and discipline students are actually looking for.
Being held to a high standard is framed as an act of care: students internalize firm expectations as evidence that the teacher takes them seriously and believes they are capable of more.
quotes: One question on every student's mind the first day of school is whether or not their teacher is a pushover. It's natural. They want to know what they can get away with, where the line is. And the answer comes easily. They just need to observe you. Your behavior always gives you away.

It's not students' first choice to goof off or do things they shouldn't in the classroom. It's just that when the teacher proves to be a pushover it's hard to resist. If they can't find inspiration and discipline from the leader of the classroom, then misbehavior becomes the next best option.
Despite some initial resistance and testing, all students want strong direction. They want boundaries. They want excellence, purpose, and motivation. They want discipline.
It feels good to be held to a high standard. Furthermore, it's proof that someone cares about them.
It's not students' first choice to goof off or do things they shouldn't in the classroom. It's just that when the teacher proves to be a pushover it's hard to resist.
